sweeps.rationale: SD1.5 and SDXL settle at different step counts, so both baselines are shown; the anime model behaves like SDXL here and would only repeat it.
sweeps.caption: How many denoising steps the sampler takes. More steps cost more time, and stop helping well before they stop costing. With an ancestral sampler like this one, changing the count also reshuffles the scene a little.

stops.caption: Two steps is barely a start: coloured mush with a hint of where things will go.
Too few steps to resolve the scene: shapes are blocky and colour smears.
Shapes are arriving, but nothing has an edge yet.
The composition arrives, but edges and faces are still soft.
Most of the scene is legible. Fine detail is not.
Detail starts to settle and small features become readable.
Nearly settled, with the sampler still moving things about between counts.
Close to this model's best for the scene; most of what you will get is here.
Little is being added now beyond what this sampler reshuffles.
The common default. Quality has levelled off even as the scene shifts.
No better than 30, and the scene has drifted again on the way.
Different, not better, for well over twice the time and kudos.

sweeps.rationale: The same step counts held on a converging sampler, so the ancestral strip's drift can be seen against a scene that settles and stays put. It matches the ancestral strip's coverage model for model and scene for scene, because the step lesson should never be one a reader can only see through a sampler that re-rolls the image underneath it.
sweeps.caption: The same step counts on a converging sampler. Once the scene settles, extra steps stop moving it.

stops.caption: Two steps: the scene has not begun to form.
Too few steps for any sampler: the scene has not resolved at all.
A shape is emerging, still without detail.
A usable image appears, though the layout is still finding itself.
The composition is nearly decided, and from here it stays put.
The final composition is in place.
Detail firms up where it already is, without the scene moving.
Locked in. From here the scene stops moving.
Indistinguishable from 20 at a glance.
Compare with the ancestral strip at 30: nothing has reshuffled since 20.
No visible change, for a third more time and kudos.
All but identical to 30, for well over twice the time and kudos.

sweeps.rationale: CFG scale controls how strongly the prompt guides the model. SDXL starts to show high-guidance damage sooner than SD1.5, so both baselines are included; the anime model behaves close enough to SDXL here that a third strip would mostly repeat the same lesson.
sweeps.caption: How strongly the model is pushed to follow your prompt. Low values give the model more freedom and may miss details you asked for. High values do not mean better prompt-following forever: they can force harsh contrast, clipped colour and brittle edges.

stops.caption: Guidance is almost off, and this is the lowest value the horde accepts. The model mostly follows its own habits, so the prompt has only a weak effect.
Very light guidance. The prompt can influence the image, but the model still has a lot of room to choose for itself.
Loose prompt-following with soft colour. Useful when you want the model to interpret the prompt rather than obey every detail.
Gentle steering, and the subject you asked for is reliably there.
A gentle balance, good when your prompt is already detailed.
Comfortable adherence with colour still behaving.
The usual home base for most models.
Firmer adherence, with contrast beginning to climb.
Firmer still, and saturation is now visibly rising.
Too much guidance is starting to show: edges become unnaturally crisp and the image looks less natural.
Over-guided: contrast is harsh, colours look burned or clipped, and edges become brittle.
Far past the useful range. The prompt is being forced so hard that the image gets worse rather than more accurate.

sweeps.rationale: Ancestral and converging samplers separate differently on each baseline, so one photoreal SD1.5 model and one SDXL model cover the contrast at fixed steps.
sweeps.caption: Which algorithm walks the image out of noise. At the same steps and seed, each one lands somewhere slightly different.

stops.caption: Fast and predictable, and a good baseline to compare the others against.
Ancestral: it adds fresh noise each step, so the image keeps changing as you add steps.
Converges quickly and is often the cleanest result at 20 to 30 steps.
Stochastic, so it lands somewhere of its own, often with richer texture.

sweeps.rationale: Two mainstream models, where 2 and 3 visibly loosen the prompt. The anime model renders this scene as a photograph and taught nothing here, so it has its own strip on the anime scene instead.
sweeps.caption: How many layers to cut from the end of the text encoder. Anime-lineage models were trained expecting one to be cut.

stops.caption: The full text encoder. What most non-anime models expect.
Skips the last layer. On an anime-lineage model this is the intended setting; elsewhere it just loosens the prompt.
Skipping further loses prompt detail, and your wording starts to be ignored.

sweeps.rationale: This strip is rendered above the model's native size because hires-fix only matters when a one-pass render is being asked to go larger than the model handles comfortably. A person makes the failure easy to see: repeated knowledge becomes a second head or extra limb, not just vague softness. The tall frame is intentional because SD1.5 often stacks a subject through a long image instead of enlarging one clean subject. The default SD1.5 model is used because the photoreal model holds together well enough to hide the lesson.
sweeps.caption: When you ask for more pixels than a model comfortably generates in one pass, it may repeat subjects or stretch shapes instead of making a larger coherent scene. Hires-fix composes a smaller image first, then enlarges it and redraws detail at the requested size.

stops.caption: Generated in one pass at the full requested size. Past the model's comfortable size, this can duplicate details, stretch anatomy, or split one subject into several.
Generated smaller first, then enlarged and redrawn. The first pass decides the composition, so the final image is more likely to stay coherent.

sweeps.rationale: The same lesson on an SDXL model, which was trained at a larger native size and fails later. SDXL did not show the problem clearly on the tall sizes used for SD1.5, so this pair uses a very large square request where one-pass generation produces duplicated anatomy. Showing both baselines matters because the failure appears at different shapes and sizes.
sweeps.caption: When you ask for more pixels than a model comfortably generates in one pass, it may repeat subjects or stretch shapes instead of making a larger coherent scene. Hires-fix composes a smaller image first, then enlarges it and redraws detail at the requested size.

stops.caption: Generated in one pass at the full requested size. Past the model's comfortable size, this can duplicate details, stretch anatomy, or split one subject into several.

sweeps.rationale: The texture strip is the one that teaches: seams are invisible on a single object and unmistakable on a repeating surface, which is what anyone actually tiles. Seam behaviour is a sampler-level effect that reads the same on every baseline, so one model is enough.
sweeps.caption: Whether the edges are made to wrap. Shown as a three-by-three plate beside the single tile, because a seam only exists where one copy meets the next.

stops.caption: The edges end wherever the image happened to stop, so every join is a hard line.
The edges are made to wrap, so the grain and the gaps run on across each join.

sweeps.rationale: The counter-example, kept deliberately: tiling is a property of the edges, not a way to make a picture repeatable. A centred object tiles into a grid of that object however the flag is set, which is the mistake the texture strip is there to correct.
sweeps.caption: The same flag on a scene with a subject in the middle. The edges do wrap, but a picture of one thing repeats as a grid of that thing either way: tiling makes edges meet, it does not make an image into a texture.

stops.caption: Repeated as-is: hard seams, and a robot in every square.
The seams are gone and the robot is still in every square. This is not what tiling is for.

sweeps.rationale: SDXL only, because the degradation being taught is SDXL-specific: it is what happens when you ask an SDXL model for the sizes an SD1.5 model was built for.
sweeps.caption: Every model has a size it was trained at. Ask an SDXL model for much less and it does not simply get smaller, it gets worse.

stops.caption: Far below anything SDXL saw in training: the image collapses into mush.
The scene survives but the subject does not: the courier is gone.
Anatomy holds, but the framing collapses to a cramped close-up of whatever fits.
Most of the scene is back. The last of the crowding clears in the next stop.
SDXL's native size. This is what the model was trained to make.

sweeps.rationale: One grid per baseline, because steps and guidance interact differently for SD1.5 and for SDXL.
sweeps.caption: Steps and guidance are not independent. Read across for guidance and down for steps: both have to be in range before an image looks right. The scene also drifts down each column: this sampler re-rolls details as steps change.

sweeps.rationale: The third baseline of the same grid, on the anime model and therefore on the anime scene: the tag idiom that lineage was trained on is part of what its guidance range means, so reading it against a photoreal prompt would measure the prompt rather than the model.
sweeps.caption: Steps and guidance are not independent. Read across for guidance and down for steps: both have to be in range before an image looks right. The scene also drifts down each column: this sampler re-rolls details as steps change.

sweeps.rationale: Which sampler to choose is really a question about how it behaves as the step count changes, and no single strip can show that. Both baselines run it because SDXL settles at different step counts than SD1.5.
sweeps.caption: Read across a row to see what more steps buy that sampler. The ancestral and SDE rows never settle: they re-roll the detail at every step count, so the image keeps changing rather than improving. The other two rows stop moving once the scene has converged. That contrast is the whole point.

sweeps.rationale: The failure this repairs is a property of the size you ask for, so it has to be read down a column of sizes rather than from a single pair. The off column doubles as the oversize anti-example: it is what asking an SD1.5 model for a large image actually looks like, duplicated subjects and all. The bottom row is four times the model's training size, past where the repair rescues anything, so the grid answers how far this carries as well as what it does. It runs on the default SD1.5 model, which breaks at oversize where the photoreal one holds together and hides the lesson.
sweeps.caption: Read down the off column to see what asking for more pixels than the model was trained on does: the scene stops being one scene and starts repeating, which on a person means a second head or a third arm. The on column generates small first, then enlarges and re-diffuses, so the composition survives the size. Read to the bottom row to see the repair run out.

rows.caption: Requested size, top to bottom. This model was trained at 512.

sweeps.rationale: The same grid an octave up. SDXL degrades more gently and later, so the sizes that show it are its own, and the bottom row is well past what any of these models were trained for.
sweeps.caption: The same lesson on a model trained at 1024. It takes a larger ask to break it, and it breaks the same way: repeated features rather than a bigger picture. The bottom row is where the second pass stops being able to compose what the first one asked for.

rows.caption: Requested size, top to bottom. This model was trained at 1024.

sweeps.rationale: The pair strip shows that the schedule matters at 10 steps; only a grid shows the part that matters more, which is that the advantage shrinks as the step count rises. Held on a converging sampler for the same reason the pair is.
sweeps.caption: Read down the rows: the gap between the two columns is wide where steps are scarce and closes as they are not. Karras is a way of spending few steps well, not a setting that is better in general.

columns.caption: The plain schedule, then the Karras one.

sweeps.rationale: Denoising strength only applies when a source image is supplied. It controls how much of that starting image is redrawn during image-to-image: low values preserve the source, middle values restyle it, and high values leave only a loose layout or ignore it entirely. Both baselines are included because SD1.5 and SDXL keep the source through slightly different ranges.
sweeps.caption: Image-to-image starts from an existing picture. Denoising strength controls how much of that picture is replaced: near 0, the source is mostly kept; around the middle, the prompt can restyle it while the subject survives; near 1, the source has little or no practical influence.

sweeps.rationale: This example uses a close portrait because negative prompts often show their effect first on fragile details such as hands and anatomy. The scene asks for bare fingers on purpose, so the improvement or failure is visible. SDXL is used because, at 512 pixels, the SD1.5 hands were too small for the lesson to read clearly.
sweeps.caption: A negative prompt names things you want the model to avoid. It is not a general quality switch: it changes the same guidance process as the main prompt, usually affecting fragile details such as hands and anatomy before anything else.
sweeps.negative_prompt: extra fingers, fused fingers, missing fingers, deformed hands, mutated hands, extra limbs, bad anatomy

stops.caption: No negative prompt: the hands are whatever the model naturally produces from the main prompt.
The same request with unwanted hand and anatomy problems named. The model is steered away from those failures, though it is not guaranteed to fix them perfectly.

sweeps.rationale: eta changes how much randomness an SDE sampler is allowed to add back during the run. Practically, low eta keeps the image closer to the deterministic version of the sampler, while higher eta lets the image wander more. The technical point being shown is that eta 0 should match the sampler's deterministic twin because no SDE noise is injected.
sweeps.caption: eta controls how much fresh noise an SDE sampler injects as it steps. At 0, no extra noise is injected and the sampler follows the same path as its deterministic twin. As eta rises, the sampler has more randomness to work with, so the image can move further from that path.

sweeps.rationale: Control strength is the one setting that really matters in the QR workflow. This scene has no straight lines in it, so the code has to be built out of cloud rather than traced over decking, and the strength is then the only thing you are looking at. Every image here was decoded with zbar before it was published. The bottom of the range came from rendering this scene at ten strengths against four seeds: 1.2 and below never scanned, on any of them; 1.25 scans on this strip's seed and is the first value shown; from 1.3 up almost every attempt scans. One seed for the whole strip, so nothing but the strength changes. The horde accepts control_strength with a control type or with the QR code workflow, so a QR request can ask for any of these values. The images here were rendered locally.
sweeps.caption: How closely the QR ControlNet makes the image follow the code it was given. Set it low and the picture takes over: the modules, the small light and dark squares a code is made of, soften into the scene until no scanner can find them. Set it high and the code takes over: it sits on the picture like printed ink. Every image here still decodes to https://aihorde.net, and the usable range is narrower than it looks.

It is not a single-variable strip and the caption must not pretend otherwise: the backends derive the second pass step count from this number, so a low stop is a lighter pass and a shorter one at once.

The enlargement is treated as a rough layout and the second pass composes its own picture at the full size. The subject survives; the scene you were refining does not.

sweeps.rationale: Denoising strength inside a mask, which is the control the masked mode adds and the one inpainting does not really have. The backend encodes the whole picture and then restricts where noise is applied, so what was under the mask is still there to be redrawn by this much; inpainting erases the masked pixels before encoding and has nothing left to vary. It runs on the deck render a reader has already met on the image-to-image page, with the coat masked and the scene's own prompt, so the only question on screen is how much of that coat survives.
sweeps.caption: The same strength control as image-to-image, acting only where the mask is. Low, and the masked part is the one that was already there; high, and it is redrawn from nothing. Everything outside the mask stays exactly as it came in at every stop.

stops.caption: Barely touched. The coat under the mask is the one that was already there.
A cleanup pass inside the mask: the same coat, tidied and lightly repainted.
The restyling band starts here, and it starts from the coat rather than from nothing.
Still recognisably the same garment, with the prompt now deciding most of its surface.
About as far as the original coat reliably survives being redrawn.
A major redraw. The cut of what was masked survives and little else does.
Almost nothing of the original coat is left beyond its silhouette.
Nothing under the mask is kept. Everywhere outside it is still untouched, which is the whole point of masking rather than lowering the strength.

sweeps.rationale: The horde has two ways to redraw part of a picture and they are different pipelines, not two names for one. Masked image-to-image encodes the whole source and restricts where noise lands, so the masked pixels are still the starting point; inpainting erases them first and grows the mask before encoding. Everything here is held apart from those two facts: one model, one source, one mask, one prompt, and one ordinary checkpoint rather than an inpainting one, because the horde runs whichever model was asked for and only requires the worker to keep an inpainting model on hand. Read across for the difference and down for where it stops mattering.
sweeps.caption: The same mask over the same picture, put through both of the horde's masked modes. The left column keeps what was under the mask and redraws it by the strength on that row, so the strength is a real dial. The right column throws it away before it starts, which is why the top right cell is a flat patch: at that strength there is not enough of the pass left to put anything back. Below the row where it can finish, inpainting does not give you a gentler edit; it gives you an unfinished one.

rows.caption: The strength asked for, top to bottom. Only the left column can act on it.

sweeps.rationale: Outpainting is the one mode with nothing of its own in the payload. The backends select the same pipeline for it as for inpainting, byte for byte, and nothing anywhere pads a canvas: the caller pads the picture and masks what it added. So these stops vary the input rather than a parameter, each one a canvas padded beforehand and checked in beside its mask, and each stating the size of its own canvas because the backend resizes a source to the requested dimensions and would otherwise squeeze the padding straight back out. What a reader is choosing is how much they are asking the model to invent, which is the only real dial here.
sweeps.caption: Pushing the edges of a picture outwards. The middle is the render the strip starts from and every stop keeps it untouched; what changes is how much new canvas the model is asked to fill on either side.

stops.caption: A narrow border each side. There is enough of the deck in view for the model to carry the railing, the canopy and the sky straight out.
Half the picture again. The scene still holds together, and the new edges are inventing rather than repeating what is beside them.

The canvas is twice what it was and half of what you are looking at was never in the original. It still reads as one place, and you can find the joins: a faint vertical seam where the picture that was sent meets the canvas around it.

sweeps.rationale: One example for each ControlNet type, all using the same source photograph. Each example shows the source image, the control map made from it, and the final image made from that map. The map is the important middle step: it shows what the model is being asked to preserve. Everything else is held constant so readers can compare what each control type keeps, what it drops, and what the model has to invent.
sweeps.caption: ControlNet works by turning the source image into a control map first. Different control types keep different information: edges, pose, depth, regions, colour, or surface direction. The final image shows what happens when the same prompt is guided by each kind of map.
sweeps.negative_prompt: photograph, 3d render, lowres, blurry, deformed hands, extra fingers, watermark, text

stops.caption: Canny makes a clean outline map of the visible edges: railing wires, mast fittings, coat folds, and the line of the hills. The final image follows those shapes closely, but it still chooses its own colour and small details, so the coat turns brown and the goggles become spectacles.

hed draws softer, thicker strokes and lets the small detail go, so the railing survives as a few bars and the face is barely described. The image keeps the pose and the horizon and takes the rest for itself: a warmer sky, a tan coat, teal in the hair.

pidinet keeps the heavy boundaries and empties out the interior, leaving the head, the coat and the railing as flat shapes. The image fills those shapes with a picture of its own, and the airship envelope comes back as a pale sail.

teed finds fine line everywhere, including the edges of the clouds and the panels of the envelope. The image follows it closely and reads as a pen drawing with colour washed over it, with the envelope drawn as a ribbed gold balloon.

pyracanny gives the same complete outline as canny with a softer edge to it. The image keeps the whole scene, down to the wires of the railing and the curve of the deck, and uses its freedom on colour.

binary reduces the photograph to black and white with no grey between, so the coat becomes one mass and the face is lost. The image invents a face to fill the gap and reads the speckle under the railing as boats on water.
scribble reduces the picture to a few coarse strokes. The image keeps the standing figure and the railing, closes the eyes it had to invent, and turns the envelope into a plain white shape.

fakescribbles traces the main shapes in thick rounded strokes and puts nothing inside them. The pose and the deck stay put, the railing comes back as wire mesh, and the goggles become an earpiece against the hair.

scribble_xdog keeps more than the other scribble modes: an inked, grainy line that still carries the folds of the coat and the rails. The image stays close to the photograph and reads as a drawing made with a dry pen.

scribble_pidinet is the loosest map here, a few beaded strokes with the interior gone. The image invents most of what it shows: rigging ropes where the mast was, birds in the sky, fur on the collar and the cuffs.

standard_lineart carries tone as well as line, so the clouds, the hills and the folds of the coat are all in the map as shading. The image stays closer to the photograph than any other line mode here and adds only small things of its own, such as the pines below the railing.

lineart draws a thin, even outline and leaves the shading out. The image keeps the composition and softens everything else, so the envelope becomes a pale balloon and a second airship appears in the distance.
lineart_anime draws a clean line and hatches the large flat areas. The image keeps the scene and answers the hatching with a ribbed envelope and a dark sea.

lineart_anime_denoise clears the faint lines away and keeps the confident ones, so the face is barely in the map at all. The image keeps the pose and the horizon and puts its own face, its own coat and a fan-shaped envelope over them.
mlsd keeps straight lines and drops almost everything else. The mast, rails, and deck edges are preserved, but the woman is not in the map, so the final image redraws her from the prompt.

Depth maps describe distance, not object identity. The figure and railing keep their relative positions, but the model decides what those shapes become, so the sea of clouds is rebuilt as water with a pale hull in it.
midas_depth reads the sky as empty and cuts the figure sharply out of it. The standing shape and the railing stay put, and the view is invented: headlands, houses and a small boat.

zoe_depth gives a flatter reading, with less distance between the figure and everything behind her. The silhouette still comes through, and the softer background fills with hills, floating ice and a ribbed envelope.
depth_anything cuts the figure out crisply and leaves the background dark. The silhouette comes through exactly, and everything behind it is the prompt's invention.

depth_anything_v2 models the folds of the coat and the curve of the envelope rather than a flat cut-out. The image follows that modelling and stays closest to the photograph of the depth modes, with the envelope drawn as a ribbed hull.

normal reports which way each surface faces, and on this photograph it comes back noisy, with the sky flattened to a single colour. The image keeps the figure and the railing and rebuilds the view behind them.

normal_bae reads the same surfaces cleanly: the shoulders, the sleeves and the folds face the way they do in the photograph. The image keeps that modelling and invents the sea, the rocks and the small boat.
OpenPose keeps the body pose and drops the surrounding scene. The stance survives, but the model has to invent the setting, so the open deck becomes the inside of a cabin.
seg turns the picture into labelled regions: figure, sky, water, deck, and so on. The final image respects those broad blocks, but the model is free to decide what appears inside them.

oneformer_ade20k gives cleaner regions than seg and separates the sky, the land, the water and the deck. The image keeps that layout band for band and invents the contents, including a village under the railing.
oneformer_coco works from coarser labels and merges what ade20k separates. The layout still comes through, and with less to go on the image makes the deck a hull and the land a bank of scrub.
color keeps the source palette but not the source shapes. The final image uses those colours to build a new scene, so the courier returns seated beside a cabin window with a box of flowers nearby.

shuffle stirs the picture into loops of itself, with her head, the railing and the ring of the airship smeared around the turns. The image keeps the colours and the round shapes and puts them somewhere new, with goggles, banks of cloud and a sea with one small boat on it.

recolor_luminance keeps the light and dark values of the source image. Because so much structure is preserved, the final image stays very close to the photograph and the requested ink-and-watercolour style barely appears.
recolor_intensity measures brightness differently and follows the picture just as closely. The image is the photograph recoloured once more, with the coat split between tan and teal.
tile gives the worker a blurred copy of the source image. The main shapes are already present, so the model mostly sharpens and repaints them in the requested style.
tile_ttplanet_guided passes the picture through almost untouched. The image repaints it line for line, and the goggles, the belt and the wires of the railing all survive the change of medium.

tile_ttplanet_simple hands over the picture with no blur at all. Nothing in this set follows the photograph more closely: the same scene, the same pose and the same light, painted rather than photographed.

sweeps.subject: anchor

sweeps.rationale: The same ControlNet types are shown on a drawing instead of a photograph. Some detectors are better suited to drawings than others: anime line detectors can find clean artwork lines here, while depth and surface detectors have less real-world volume to read. Anything Diffusion is used at clip skip 2 because ControlNet runs on SD1.5, and this prompt uses the anime tag style that model expects.
sweeps.caption: The source is a drawing, so the control maps behave differently than they did on the photograph. Line-based maps have cleaner artwork to follow; depth and surface maps have less physical scene information to extract.
sweeps.negative_prompt: lowres, worst quality, bad anatomy, bad hands, extra digits, watermark, signature, photorealistic, 3d, cg

stops.caption: Canny outlines everything in the drawing: the ears, the strands at the edge of the hair, the steps and the fallen leaves. The image the worker made matches it shape for shape and changes only what an outline cannot say, so the hair comes back silver and the maples lose their fire.

hed keeps the heavy strokes and lets the small ones go, so the leaves and the stonework are only suggested. The seated pose and the pillars stay put, and the image puts a warmer autumn back into the scene.
pidinet keeps only the strong boundaries, and the face and the folds of the haori go with the rest. The image keeps the seated shape and the steps and paints its own face and its own gold sash.
teed finds fine line everywhere, including each maple leaf on the stone. The image follows it closely and gives the most detailed reading of the drawing in this set, down to the wet steps.
pyracanny outlines as completely as canny with a softer edge to it. The image keeps the whole scene and uses its freedom on colour, which drains to grey with the red of the hakama kept.

binary reduces the drawing to black and white, and the face, the hair and the fox tail fall into one mass. The image keeps the seated figure and the pillars and rebuilds the trees as a shrine in mist.
scribble leaves a coarse black and white reduction of the picture. The pose and the steps survive, and the maples behind are replaced with a corridor of torii gates.
fakescribbles traces the main shapes in thick rounded strokes. The seated figure stays put, and the trees become a wall of gates in fog.
scribble_xdog leaves a fine grainy line that still carries the folds of the cloth and the edges of the steps. The image stays close to the drawing and sets props of its own on the stone.
scribble_pidinet gives the loosest strokes here and loses the boundary between the figure and the ground. The image keeps the pose and dresses it differently, in black over white.
standard_lineart carries shading as well as line, so the trees, the steps and the cloth all have weight in the map. The image stays close to the drawing and warms the maples to pink.
lineart draws a thin even line and leaves the shading out. The image keeps the pose, the steps and the dark hair the drawing has, and lets the season drift towards pink.

lineart_anime draws the clean line this kind of drawing was made for, and it catches the ears, the tail and the fall of the hair. The image keeps all of it and changes little more than the colour of the maples.
lineart_anime_denoise clears the faint lines away first, so the map is sparser. The image keeps the pose and the steps and adds furniture of its own, including a pair of standing lanterns.

mlsd finds the pillars, the crossbeam and the edges of the steps, and finds nothing of the girl or the fox. The image keeps that architecture and builds a different picture inside it, with the figure seen from behind on a long stair.
depth reports distance alone, and here it does keep the ears and the tail as part of the near shape. The image keeps that silhouette and rebuilds the gates, the trees and the leaves around it.
midas_depth separates the figure from a flat dark background. The seated shape stays put and the setting is invented, with red cloth laid across the steps.
zoe_depth reads the scene more softly, with the tail barely separated from the stone. The image keeps the shape and gives the background less structure than the other depth modes do.
depth_anything cuts the figure, the ears and the tail out cleanly. The silhouette comes through exactly, and the railing, the trees and the mist behind it are the image's own.
depth_anything_v2 models the hair and the folds rather than a flat cut-out, and the image follows it closely. It gives the truest seat and posture of the depth modes on this drawing.
normal comes back noisy on a drawing that has no real lighting in it, with flat patches where it could not decide. The image still keeps the figure and invents a shrine roof and a hanging lantern.

normal_bae is soft and almost featureless here, because a flat illustration gives a surface detector very little to read. The image keeps the pose loosely, adds a large bow, and moves the scene indoors.
openpose finds the body and nothing else: no ears, no tail, no shrine. The seat and the reach of the arm stay put, and everything that makes her a fox keeper comes from the prompt.
seg labels the picture into regions and mislabels several of them on a drawing. The image keeps the block layout and reads the steps as the floor of a wooden hall.
oneformer_ade20k gives clean regions: the figure, the two pillars, the ground and the trees. The image keeps that arrangement and fills the trees with a corridor of gates.
oneformer_coco labels the same scene more coarsely and loses the figure into one flat shape. The layout still comes through, and the image puts its own keeper and its own maples inside it.

color keeps a grid of the drawing's colours and none of its shapes: white, vermilion, cream and a little navy. The image spends that palette on an arrangement of its own, a row of torii running back into the trees, and gives the keeper white hair along with everything else.

shuffle stirs the drawing into loops of itself, the maples and the black hair wound around white spirals. The image takes the same colours into a colder scene, with pale trees behind the gate and the keeper sitting silver-haired on the steps.
recolor_luminance is the drawing in grey with every tone intact, so the image has only the colour left to decide. It returns the scene exactly, with the black hair and the red hakama the drawing has.
recolor_intensity measures brightness differently and follows the picture just as closely. The colour comes back thinner here, with a gold sash and pale leaves.
tile hands over a blurred copy of the drawing itself. The image sharpens it back and paints in the detail the blur had lost, including the grain of the steps and the leaves on them.
tile_ttplanet_guided passes the drawing through almost unchanged. The image repaints it faithfully and sets shrine buildings behind the trees.
tile_ttplanet_simple hands over the picture untouched, and the image is the drawing again in ink and wash, with the same pose, the same tail and the same fallen leaves.

sweeps.subject: anchor

sweeps.rationale: This third source image shows what happens when a control type has little or nothing to detect. There is no human body, so the pose detector returns an empty map. The scene is close, soft, and shallow, so depth detectors have less distance to separate than they had in the airship deck example. For readers choosing a control type, seeing a weak or empty map is more useful than only seeing successful cases.
sweeps.caption: Not every control type can read every source image. This example shows the failure cases directly: pose has no body to find, and depth has only a shallow close-up scene to work from.
sweeps.negative_prompt: photograph, 3d render, lowres, blurry, deformed, watermark, text

stops.caption: Canny outlines the whole rooftop: the ports in the robot's shell, the leaves growing from its head, the pots and the skyline. The image the worker made keeps every one of them in place and repaints the scene in ink and wash.
hed keeps the heavy strokes and lets the fine ones go. The shell and the pots stay put, and with the small detail gone the image reads the three lens ports as a face and gives them eyes.
pidinet keeps the boundaries and empties the interior. The image answers with a cartoon, putting two eyes, a nose and a mouth where the ports and the seams were.
teed finds fine line across the whole picture, including the foliage and the water at the tap. The image follows it closely and keeps the machine looking like a machine.
pyracanny outlines as completely as canny with a softer edge to it. The image keeps the pots, the planters and the skyline exactly while painting them freely.
binary flattens a sunset photograph into black and white and loses the markings on the shell. The image keeps the shape, paints the body pale, and puts a brush where the tap was.
scribble leaves a few coarse strokes and no surface at all. The image turns the machine into a character with a face and wheels and keeps only the pots and the skyline from the photograph.
fakescribbles traces the main shapes in thick rounded strokes. The stance and the pots stay put, the shell comes back green, and the lens ports become eyes again.
scribble_xdog keeps a finer, grainier line and more of the surface with it. The image stays closer to the machine and sets sunflowers over its head.
scribble_pidinet gives beaded strokes that lose the edge of the robot altogether. The image invents the most here: a smiling face, blue gloves and a row of pots.
standard_lineart carries the shading as well as the line. The image keeps the shell, the arms and the pots and repaints the metal in blue.
lineart draws a thin even line and leaves the tone out. The image keeps the three ports, the plants and the planters, and the shell stays orange.
lineart_anime keeps a clean line over the whole picture. The image keeps the machine and the rooftop and reads them as a drawing rather than a photograph.
lineart_anime_denoise drops the faint lines and keeps the strong ones. The image keeps the shape and the pots and puts sunflowers where the photograph has leaves.

mlsd finds the roof edges, the planters and the buildings, and finds nothing of the robot at all. The rooftop comes back exactly and the machine is rebuilt from the prompt as something else, with a helmet for a head and an apron over its body.
depth gives the rounded mass of the robot and the lumps of the plants without a single marking. The image keeps the volumes and paints a smiling face onto them.
midas_depth reads the same volumes more coarsely. The image keeps the round body and puts one large eye where the map left a shadow.
zoe_depth flattens the scene, with the robot barely separated from the pots. The image keeps the mass and gives it a single green eye, because the map never said there were three ports.
depth_anything separates the robot and the plants crisply. The three ports come back and the shell keeps the photograph's shape, with the colour left to the prompt.
depth_anything_v2 models the dome and the leaves rather than a flat cut-out. It gives the most faithful robot of the depth modes, orange again and with all three lenses.
normal comes back noisy on this photograph, with the sky flattened to a single colour. The image still keeps the shell, the arms and the pots and repaints the rooftop behind them.

normal_bae reads the dome, the arms and the pots as surfaces facing where they face in the photograph. The image keeps that modelling and changes little more than the colour of the lenses and the plants.
openpose found no person here, so the map it drew is empty black. With nothing to follow, the image keeps only what the prompt asked for and builds a different machine on a different rooftop.
seg labels the picture and splits the robot across several regions, so the shell comes back in pieces. The image keeps the pots and the greenery in place and reassembles the machine its own way.
oneformer_ade20k reads the robot as one region, with the sky, the hedges and the floor around it. The image keeps that arrangement and paints a wide-eyed machine into the shape.
oneformer_coco has no label that fits a gardening robot, so it hands over a shape among the foliage. The layout stays put, and the image fills the shape with a crowned machine and hoses for arms.

color keeps a grid of the picture's colours and none of its shapes: cream across the top, orange and brown through the middle, one square of bright blue. The image gives that palette to a different machine, orange shelled with a blue arm and a blue wheel, clipping a bed of plants.

shuffle stirs the photograph into loops of itself, shell, lenses and leaves wound round the sunset. The image keeps every colour and spends it on another robot, pale green in the body with orange rings painted across it and the city behind gone hazy.

recolor_luminance is the photograph in grey with every tone kept, which leaves the image only the colour to choose. It comes back as the photograph again, orange shell and blue lenses, with none of the ink and wash the prompt asked for.
recolor_intensity measures brightness differently and follows the picture just as closely. The result is the same photograph once more, with cooler colour in it.

tile hands over a heavily blurred copy of the picture. Every shape is already there and the work left is to put the detail back, which the image does in ink and wash, with flowers and grass where the blur said nothing.
tile_ttplanet_guided passes the picture through almost untouched, and the image repaints it faithfully: the same shell, the same three lenses and the same pots, in the medium the prompt asked for.
tile_ttplanet_simple hands over the picture with no blur at all, and nothing in this set follows it more closely. The image is the rooftop again, painted instead of photographed.

sweeps.subject: anchor

sweeps.rationale: The same 33 detectors on a building instead of a person. Straight edges, rows of windows and a deep perspective are what the line and edge detectors were built for, and a structure has none of the things a pose detector looks for. Reading this beside the other two sources in world 1 is how the choice of detector stops being a list of names and becomes a question about the picture in front of you.
sweeps.caption: The source is a building: straight edges, repeated windows, and a long run of perspective. Edge and line detectors have a great deal to hold on to here, and the detectors that look for a body find nothing.
sweeps.negative_prompt: photograph, 3d render, lowres, blurry, deformed hands, extra fingers, watermark, text

stops.caption: Canny traces the building's outlines: the girders, the window openings, the edges of the stairs. The image that comes back stands the same structure in the same place and paints it in the weather the prompt asked for.
hed draws thicker, softer strokes than Canny. The frame and the roofline survive, the small fittings do not. The image follows the mass of the building and invents its surface.
pidinet keeps a moderate amount of the building: the main uprights and the roof, with some of the smaller structure. The image holds the shape and takes the colour and the light for itself.
teed draws dense, soft edges, so most of the building's structure reaches the map. The image follows it closely and changes the hour and the weather rather than the shape.
pyracanny finds more of the building than Canny does, including faint edges in the distance. More of the background survives into the image as a result.

Binary splits the picture into black and white at a brightness threshold. A building of lit and shaded faces splits into large solid blocks, so the map is areas rather than lines, and the image reads them as masses of light and dark.
Scribble finds a great deal in a building: it marks far more of this picture than it marked of the character picture. The image gets a loose, sketched version of the same structure to follow.
fakescribbles draws the building as rough strokes, dropping the fine structure. The image keeps the silhouette and the main lines and fills the rest in.
scribble_xdog draws a thin, sparse tracing of the building. The image keeps the main shape and is free with everything else.
scribble_pidinet marks the building broadly, including a lot of the background. The image follows the whole scene rather than the structure alone.
standard_lineart draws the building as clean, even lines: uprights, cross-bracing, the roof. The image reads it as a drawing to paint over.
lineart finds more of the building than it finds of the character picture, because straight edges are what it is good at. The image follows those lines and re-lights the scene.
lineart_anime is built for drawn artwork, and it still reads a building's straight edges cleanly. The map is sparser than standard lineart's, so the image invents more.
lineart_anime_denoise drops the faint marks and keeps the confident ones, so the map is the building's main structure only. The image fills in the detail it lost.

mlsd looks for straight lines and nothing else, which is exactly what a building is made of. It finds more of them here than in the character picture, and the image gets the frame of the structure to build on.
The depth map reads the building as a solid nearer the viewer with the sky behind. The image keeps that arrangement and re-invents the surfaces.
midas_depth separates the building from its background, though it is vaguer about the structure inside it. The image holds the mass and the distance and makes up the detail.
zoe_depth reads the run of distance through the picture and keeps the building standing out of it. The image follows that sense of depth.
depth_anything gives a smoother reading than the older depth detectors: the building is one mass at one distance. The image keeps that and invents its surface.
depth_anything_v2 marks the building's distance and the ground it stands on. The image holds the arrangement and changes the light.
The normal map says which way each surface faces. On a building that means broad flat planes and few curves. The image builds a scene from those planes.
normal_bae reads a building as a small number of flat faces, so the map is much plainer than it is on the character picture. The image gets the arrangement of surfaces and little else.
openpose looks for a human body. There is no body in this picture, so the map is empty and the image is what the prompt alone would make.

The segmentation map labels each part of the picture: building, sky, ground. A building gives fewer and larger regions than the character picture does, and the image fills each one with something of that kind.
oneformer_ade20k labels the picture by region. It finds the building, the sky and the ground here, and the image puts something of each kind back in the same place.
oneformer_coco marks a few large regions on a building: the structure, the sky, the ground. The image follows the layout of those regions rather than any edge.
The colour map is the picture blurred down to its colours. A building holds its palette in large blocks, so the image gets a strong steer on where each colour goes.
Shuffle stirs the picture's colours into a swirl. The image keeps that palette and arranges the building however the prompt suggests.
recolor_luminance throws the colour away and keeps the brightness. The image is the same building, repainted: the structure barely moves.
recolor_intensity keeps a slightly different reading of brightness. The image stays close to the building and changes its colours.
Tile keeps almost the whole picture as the map, so the image is the same building again with new detail worked into it.
tile_ttplanet_guided holds the building tightly and lets the prompt add detail. The image is a cleaner version of the same picture.
tile_ttplanet_simple holds the building just as tightly, with a plainer reading of it. The image stays very close to the source.

sweeps.subject: building

sweeps.rationale: The same 33 detectors on a flat drawing: solid blocks of colour, no shading, no gradients. Half of these detectors read light and shade to work out what is in front of what, and there is none here for them to read. The prompt then asks for the world's normal painted look, so what each map carried across is visible in the result.
sweeps.caption: The source is flat colour with no shading in it at all. Detectors that trace outlines still find their shapes; detectors that read light and shade to judge distance and surface direction have nothing to work from.
sweeps.negative_prompt: photograph, 3d render, lowres, blurry, deformed hands, extra fingers, watermark, text

stops.caption: There is little for Canny to trace in flat colour. It marks well under half as much of this picture as it marks of the character picture, so the map is a few outlines around the big shapes, and the image invents everything inside them.
hed finds the boundaries between the blocks of colour and almost nothing else. The image treats those few soft strokes as the outline of a scene and paints the rest.
pidinet marks the edges between colour blocks. The map is sparse, and the image keeps the layout while making up the surface and the light.
teed needs texture to draw densely, and there is none here. It marks far less than it does in the character picture, and the image fills the space with detail of its own.
pyracanny finds under half as much here as it does in the character picture. The image keeps the big shapes and invents the rest.

Binary splits the picture into black and white at a brightness threshold. Flat colour splits cleanly into solid areas, so the map is large blocks rather than lines, and the image reads them as masses of light and dark.
Scribble draws around each block of colour, so the map is bolder than the edge detectors manage here. The image gets clear shapes to work from and paints them with light the source never had.
fakescribbles marks the boundaries between the flat areas as rough strokes. The image keeps that arrangement and invents the surface.
scribble_xdog needs fine detail to work with, and flat colour has none. The map is very sparse and the image is mostly the prompt's own.
scribble_pidinet still marks the edges between the colour blocks. The image follows those shapes and fills them with texture the source does not have.
standard_lineart draws the outlines of the flat shapes. The map is thinner than the one it draws from the character picture, and the image paints inside those outlines as it likes.
lineart has only the boundaries between colours to find, far less than the building gives it. The image keeps the shapes and invents their surface.
